name: Oklahoma Campground
note: USFS Gifford Pinchot NF (Mt. Adams RD) campground in old-growth hemlock/cedar along the Little White Salmon River near the Columbia Gorge; ~15 drive-in standard non-electric sites (site 12/13 a tent-only double), no hookups, potable water + vault toilets, unpaved lumpy spurs. Concessionaire-run, reservable online mid-May to mid-Sept; recreation.gov lists sites for RVs up to 40 ft (sites described as large/spacious; an older FS figure says 22 ft). --Claude

name: Moss Creek Campground
note: USFS Gifford Pinchot NF (Mt. Adams RD) campground shaded by hemlock/cedar/fir along the Little White Salmon River (which borders it on two sides), ~1,400 ft; 16 drive-in sites, no hookups, drinking water + vault toilets, max RV length 32 ft. Concessionaire-run, reservable online mid-May to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Takhlakh Lake Campground
note: 54-site Gifford Pinchot NF campground on Takhlakh Lake at the NW base of Mt. Adams; back-in unpaved spurs 15-40 ft, vault toilets, no hookups; mix of reservable and FCFS sites (10 tent-only). Renowned Mt. Adams reflection over the lake; electric-motor/paddle boating only. Open mid-July to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Killen Creek Campground
note: 9-site first-come, first-served Gifford Pinchot NF campground in a high lodgepole/silver-fir stand near the Mt. Adams Wilderness (Killen Creek trailhead); vault toilets, no water, no hookups, on-site Scan-and-Pay. Drive-in sites reportedly to ~22 ft. Popular climbers'/hikers' basecamp. Open mid-May to mid-Sept. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Hood Park
note: 67-site USACE campground near the Snake-Columbia confluence (Lake Wallula, McNary pool) at Burbank/Pasco; all sites 50-amp electric (no water/sewer at site), paved drives, many pull-through accommodating large RVs, flush toilets, hot showers, dump station with potable fill, boat ramp and swim beach. Reservable online; open mid-May to early Sept. --Claude

name: Charbonneau Park
note: USACE (Walla Walla District) park on a wooded peninsula in Lake Sacajawea (Snake River, Ice Harbor Dam), off Hwy 124/Monument Dr near Burbank. 52 family sites with electric hookups (some full hookup); flush toilets, showers, dump station, boat launch/marina, swim area, playground. Reservable online; open mid-May-early Sept. Several sites overlook the lake. --Claude

name: Fishhook Park
note: USACE (Walla Walla District) park on a wooded peninsula in Lake Sacajawea (Snake River, Ice Harbor Dam), ~5 mi off US-12 near Prescott. 41 family sites with 50-amp electric + water hookups, plus 11 primitive walk-up tent sites; flush toilets, showers, dump station, boat launch, swim area. Reservable online; open mid-May-early Sept. --Claude

name: Teal Spring Campground
note: Small USFS campground (Umatilla NF, Pomeroy RD) on Skyline Drive (FR 40) in the Blue Mountains at ~5640 ft, with views over the Tucannon drainage and Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness. 14 sites, roughly half tent-only and half tent/trailer; vault toilets, picnic tables, no potable water. Gravel forest-road access, open ~May-Nov. First-come, first-served (fee). --Claude

name: Alder Thicket Campground
note: Small USFS campground (Umatilla NF, Pomeroy RD) just off FR 40 about 3 mi into the Blue Mountains at ~5110 ft, shaded by alder. Tent camping on the lower area plus RV/trailer dry-camping space at the top; vault toilet, picnic tables, no potable water, no hookups. Gravel access, open ~May-Nov. First-come, first-served (fee). --Claude

name: Misery Spring Campground
note: Small free USFS campground (Umatilla NF, Pomeroy RD) high on the Blue Mountains ridge at ~6170 ft, with panoramic views into the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness. 5 primitive tent/trailer sites; vault toilet, picnic tables, no potable water, no hookups. Gravel FR 40 then FR 4030/4030-20 spur access (rough in spots); open ~June-Nov. First-come, first-served (free). --Claude

name: Godman Campground
note: Small primitive Umatilla NF campground/trailhead (Pomeroy Ranger District) high in the Blue Mountains on Kendall Skyline Rd; 8 sites (3 tent/trailer, 5 tent-only). No fee, first-come first-served. Vault toilet and picnic tables; no potable water. Gravel-road access, open roughly late June-Oct. Also a Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness trailhead (offers horse sites). --Claude

name: Iron Creek Campground
note: Gifford Pinchot NF campground (Cowlitz Valley Ranger District) at the Iron Creek-Cispus River confluence, ~1,200 ft; 99 back-in paved sites in old-growth, max vehicle 40 ft, drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups. Reservable on recreation.gov, normally open mid-May-mid-Sep. Closed for the 2026 season for windstorm cleanup (many downed trees) - verify reopening before visiting. --Claude

name: North Fork Campground
note: Gifford Pinchot NF (Cowlitz Valley RD) campground on the North Fork Cispus River, ~11 mi SE of Randle. Individual sites take RVs to 32 ft; no hookups, vault toilets, drinking water. Reservable online, open mid-May to mid-Sept. (Three group sites cap at 22 ft, separate.) --Claude

name: Blue Lake Creek Campground
note: Gifford Pinchot NF (Cowlitz Valley RD) campground along Blue Lake Creek near the Cispus River, popular with OHV riders on the adjacent Valley Trail system. 11 back-in sites with paved spurs 20-40 ft; no hookups, vault toilets, no drinking water. Reservable online, late May-Sept. --Claude

name: Columbia Hills Historical State Park (Horsethief Lake)
note: WA State Park on Horsethief Lake, a Columbia River backwater east of The Dalles. 4 standard and 8 partial-hookup (electric/water) drive-in sites plus 4 walk-in and 2 hiker/biker sites; ~10 sites fit RVs 20-35 ft, max 60 ft (limited). Reservable May-Sept then FCFS; campground/lake closed late Oct-late March. --Claude

name: Bruceport County Park
note: Pacific County park on a bluff overlooking Willapa Bay, about 5 mi south of South Bend off US-101. Seasonal (approx. April-December); 42 sites with a mix of full-hookup (30/50-amp, water, sewer), partial-hookup, and primitive/no-hookup RV sites plus tent sites, free hot showers, dump station; reservable by phone/email. --Claude

name: Whitehorse Regional Park Campground
note: Snohomish County campground on North Mountain Rd just outside Darrington (near the Whitehorse Trail). 30 sites in 3 loops: Loop 1 (sites 1-13) full-utility water/50-amp/sewer back-in & pull-through for all RV sizes; Loop 2 equestrian; Loop 3 (19-30) tent-only. Dump station, ADA showers, picnic shelter. Closed/winterized mid-Oct to mid-Mar. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Bates State Park
note: Oregon State Parks campground at the old mill townsite of Bates along the Middle Fork John Day River. 28 primitive sites for tents or self-contained RVs plus a 6-site hiker/biker camp; vault toilets, potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (no reservations). Open seasonally ~May 1-Oct. --Claude

name: Jackson F. Kimball State Recreation Site
note: Primitive Oregon State Parks recreation site at the spring-fed headwaters of the Wood River, ~3 mi N of Fort Klamath. 10 primitive drive-in sites (plus 2 primitive horse sites); vault toilet, fire rings, picnic tables, NO potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served. Open ~May-Nov, weather permitting. --Claude

name: Cove Palisades State Park — Deschutes River Campground
note: Deschutes River Campground at Cove Palisades State Park on Lake Billy Chinook — 87 full-hookup RV sites (A/C loops) + 93 tent sites with water nearby (B loop), set into high-desert terrain with boulders; RVs to 50 ft. Open ~May–mid-Sep. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Minam State Recreation Area

season.note: Water Memorial Day through September; OPRD publishes no camping dates.

note: Minam State Recreation Area on the Wallowa River near its confluence with the Minam River — 22 primitive sites (drinking water, no hookups); back-in slots plus a few spots right by the river fit RVs. Reached by a narrow gravel road that is tight for big rigs. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: McCubbins Gulch Campground
note: Mt. Hood National Forest (USFS, Barlow RD) rustic campground about 25 miles west of Maupin off County Rd 216 / FR 2110. ~15 first-come, first-served sites (no hookups), vault toilet, many sites adjacent to McCubbins Creek; vehicles 25 ft max. Within the McCubbins Gulch OHV trail area (expect OHV noise); seasonal, roughly May-Sept. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Memaloose State Park

season.note: Water may stay off and restrooms closed until mid to late March; OPRD publishes no camping dates.

note: Oregon State Parks campground in the Columbia River Gorge near Mosier, accessible only from I-84 westbound (Memaloose rest area). ~110 sites including full-hookup and tent sites; overlooks the Columbia River but no river access from the campground (active Union Pacific rail line between). Reservable online. --Claude

name: River Bridge Campground
note: USFS Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (High Cascades RD) on the Upper Rogue River off FR 6210 near Prospect; 9 single sites + 2 OHV sites, RVs/trailers OK, vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served (cashless Scan-and-Pay as of 7/2026); open ~May-Nov. --Claude

name: Silver Creek Marsh Campground
note: USFS Fremont-Winema NF (Silver Lake RD) general campground with horse corrals on Silver Creek; 15 level, well-shaded sites, RVs to 25 ft, vault toilets, potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served; open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Jones Creek Campground
note: Oregon Dept. of Forestry campground in Tillamook State Forest on the Wilson River near the Tillamook Forest Center; 28 first-come drive-in sites (some fit RVs, no hookups) plus 14 walk-in sites and 1 reservable group site. Open ~mid-May to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Ukiah-Dale Forest State Scenic Corridor
note: Oregon State Parks campground along US-395 on Camas Creek near the North Fork John Day River, southwest of Ukiah; 27 primitive first-come sites (a few with electric), flush toilets, paved parking pads, fire rings. Open ~May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Catherine Creek State Park
note: Oregon State Parks campground on Catherine Creek southeast of Union in the Wallowa foothills; 20 first-come sites, parking accommodates self-contained RVs, flush toilets, potable water, firewood for sale. Open ~May to early Oct. --Claude

name: Beachside State Recreation Site
note: Oregon State Parks oceanfront campground on US-101 south of Waldport, right behind the beach dune. 32 electrical sites with water plus 42 tent sites and 2 yurts; max RV length listed to 40 ft. Reservable via ReserveAmerica; open seasonally mid-March to late October. Dump stations at South Beach or Washburne SP. --Claude

name: Daley Creek Campground
note: Small USFS campground (Rogue River-Siskiyou NF, High Cascades RD) near the confluence of Beaver Dam and Daley Creeks off Dead Indian Memorial Hwy / FR 37. 6 sites (3 tent, 3 designated trailer sites), vault toilet, no potable water, pack-out trash; drive-in on maintained gravel forest road. First-come, first-served, $8/night, open ~June-Oct. --Claude

name: Mount Ashland Campground
note: Rustic USFS campground (Klamath NF, on the Siskiyou crest in Oregon) 1 mi south of Mt. Ashland Ski Resort, ~10.5 mi up FR 20 from I-5. 9 sites accommodating small RVs/trailers to ~28 ft, no potable water, pack-out trash. First-come, first-served, open ~June-Oct once FR 20 clears of snow; elev ~6,600 ft. --Claude

name: Wildcat Campground
note: BLM campground in the Hyatt Lake Recreation Area east of Ashland, on the west side of Hyatt Reservoir. 12 sites in an open setting, well hand-pump water, vault toilets, undeveloped boat launch; accommodates RVs and tents. Reservable on recreation.gov, $7/night, open ~late May-Oct 1. --Claude

name: Anthony Lake Campground
note: High-elevation USFS campground (Wallowa-Whitman NF, Elkhorn Range) directly adjacent to Anthony Lake at ~7,100 ft. 30+ sites among boulders/conifers, paved parking aprons, no hookups or dump; max RV/trailer length modest (many sites ~20-22 ft). Reservable on recreation.gov, open ~July-Sept. Temporarily within the 2026 Anthony Fire area closure (seasonal, not permanent). --Claude

name: Millers Lane Campground
note: USFS campground (Wallowa-Whitman NF) on the south shore of Phillips Reservoir in open ponderosa pine, off Hudspeth Lane / FR 2220. 11 tent/trailer sites plus 4 tent-only, vault toilets, no potable water; managed by the Anthony Lakes Campgrounds concessionaire, $12/night, open ~May-Sept. --Claude

name: South Fork Campground
note: USFS campground (Wallowa-Whitman NF, Unity RD) along the South Fork of the Burnt River, ~7.5 mi west of Unity on FR 6005. 12 tent/trailer sites plus 2 tent-only, reconstructed 2008 with pull-through trailer parking under pine/fir; popular for fishing and Blue Mountain OHV trails. Reservable on recreation.gov, ~$15/night, open ~May-Nov; elev ~4,400 ft. --Claude

name: Southwest Shore Campground
note: USFS campground (Wallowa-Whitman NF) on the southwest shore of Phillips Reservoir in warm open ponderosa pine, off Hudspeth Lane / FR 2220. 16 tent/trailer sites; usually the first of the three Phillips Lake campgrounds to open in spring. Managed by the Anthony Lakes Campgrounds concessionaire, open ~May-Sept. --Claude

name: Union Creek Campground
note: Large USFS campground (Wallowa-Whitman NF) on the north shore of Phillips Reservoir, ~18 mi south of Baker City. 60+ tent/trailer sites on three loops (some full hookups, some water/electric) plus group sites; paved/gravel spurs large enough for any size RV, dump station, flush toilets, boat launch and swim beach. Reservable on recreation.gov, open ~May-Sept. --Claude

name: Crane Prairie Campground
note: Deschutes NF campground on the east shore of Crane Prairie Reservoir off the Cascade Lakes Scenic Byway. 130 sites total (124 accommodate RVs/trailers 24-90 ft, 6 tent-only), no hookups; paved roads and most spurs, vault toilets, drinking water, boat ramp/marina nearby. Reservable online, open mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Frissell Crossing Campground
note: USFS Willamette NF (McKenzie River RD) campground on the South Fork McKenzie River at ~2,600 ft, built 1934 by the CCC. 11 sites, RVs 20-50 ft; vault toilets, fire rings, hand-pump water. Reservable online (typically late Apr-early Sept). --Claude

name: Jack Creek Campground
note: Deschutes National Forest (Sisters RD) campground on spring-fed Jack Creek, west of Camp Sherman near Suttle Lake. 19 sites accommodating RVs to 40 ft, picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups; open mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable on recreation.gov (FCFS late season). --Claude

name: Fan Creek Recreation Site
note: BLM Northwest Oregon District, Nestucca River Recreation Area, along the Nestucca River in the Coast Range. 11 standard sites + a group shelter, each with picnic table, fire ring and paved parking; 2 vault toilets, well water (potable, may be off in low season). $15/night, reservable online or pay-on-arrival via the rec.gov app (no cell service). Season ~May-Sep; tent and small/mid RV. --Claude

name: Scott Creek Campground
note: USFS Fremont-Winema NF, remote camp reached via ~6 mi of dirt road off US-97 (Military Crossing/Sun Mountain Rd). 6 sites shaded by lodgepole, ponderosa and white fir; picnic table/fire ring, one vault toilet, no potable water. No posted max RV length; dirt access can be rough when wet. First-come, first-served. Open ~5/15-mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Mona Campground
note: USFS Willamette NF (McKenzie River RD) campground on the NE shore of Blue River Reservoir, ~51 mi E of Eugene. 23 sites (20 single, 3 double) with paved road and spurs, mostly flat; drinking water, vault toilets, firewood for sale. FS lists max trailer 36 ft. Reservable via recreation.gov May-mid Sept. --Claude

name: Sandbeach Campground (Sand Lake Recreation Area)
note: USFS Siuslaw NF campground in the Sand Lake Recreation Area (coastal dunes OHV area, Hebo RD), 81 standard nonelectric sites with paved parking aprons; flush toilets, drinking water, OHV loading ramp; no hookups/dump; max RV length ~40 ft. Reservation-only May-Oct on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Pine Meadows Campground (Cottage Grove Lake)
note: USACE campground on the east shore of Cottage Grove Lake (~95 sites incl. primitive A-O loop). No hookups but big-rig friendly (rigs to ~105 ft); flush toilets, showers, dump station, swim area, playground. Reservable on recreation.gov, mid-May to mid-Sept. Alcohol prohibited on all Cottage Grove Lake COE lands. --Claude

name: Mallard Marsh Campground
note: Deschutes NF (Bend-Fort Rock RD) campground next to Hosmer Lake on the Cascade Lakes Scenic Byway; 14 standard nonelectric sites (max spur ~40 ft per FS page; some sources list ~26 ft), vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups. Fly-fishing lake. Reservable online (late May-late Sep). --Claude

name: Sharps Creek Recreation Site
note: BLM (Northwest Oregon District) campground alongside Sharps Creek, 12 sites, no hookups, vault toilets and running water, swimming hole; sites accommodate RVs (roughly to 25-40 ft per sources). Open Memorial Day through early fall; half reservable online, half FCFS. --Claude

name: Knebal Springs Campground
note: Mt. Hood NF (Barlow RD) small drive-in campground in a Ponderosa pine setting adjacent Knebal Springs Trail; 7-8 sites (3 with horse corrals), vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups. Max vehicle length 22 ft (borderline for a 23-ft rig). First-come, first-served. Season late May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Coyote Campground
note: Wallowa-Whitman NF drive-in campground in open pine forest and grassland off NF-46 (gravel access); ~6-9 tent/trailer sites, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served. Season June-Sept. Satellite shows open grassy pull-ins that fit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Dougherty Campground
note: Rustic Wallowa-Whitman NF (Hells Canyon NRA) campground in open pine/grassland near Billy Meadows: 12 sites (4 tent/trailer, 8 tent-only), vault toilet, no water, no hookups. Reached via ~40 mi of maintained gravel forest roads (FR 46) off Hwy 3 north of Enterprise. First-come, first-served, $10/night self-pay; season ~June-early Oct. --Claude

name: Irondyke Forest Camp
note: Primitive 5-site Wallowa-Whitman NF camp along the Wild & Scenic Lostine River (~5,200 ft), picnic table + fire ring, vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups. Accessed via Lostine River Road/FR 8210 (paved then rough, narrow, washboard gravel) - passable by smaller rigs (horse trailers use it) but tight for big RVs. First-come, first-served, $10/night self-pay; season ~June-Sept. --Claude

name: Armstrong Campground
note: Mt. Hood NF campground on the Wild & Scenic Clackamas River off Hwy 224 east of Estacada: 11-12 sites, RVs to ~26 ft (interior roads tight for larger rigs), vault toilet, drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, ~$18/night; open ~April-Oct. Riverside Fire (2020) damage - watch for hazard trees. --Claude

name: Hoodview Campground
note: Mt. Hood NF campground on the south shore of Timothy Lake beneath Mt. Hood: ~43 single-family sites for tents/trailers/RVs to ~35 ft, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Fully reservable online, ~$24-32/night; season ~late May-Sept. --Claude

name: Olallie Meadow Campground
note: USFS (Mt. Hood NF) at ~4,500 ft beside Olallie Meadow, reached via ~3 mi of gravel (FR 4690) then FR 4220. 7-site first-come, first-served campground, max vehicle 24 ft, no hookups, open ~mid-June-mid-Sept (snow-gated). First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Stone Creek Campground
note: 43 sites in two loops on the southeast shore of Timothy Lake, Mt. Hood NF, ~3,270 ft; 22 RV-sized non-electric sites plus 21 tent sites; vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Reservable on recreation.gov; open roughly Memorial Day through mid-September. --Claude

name: Fish Lake Campground (Steens Mountain)
note: BLM (Burns District, Steens Mountain CMPA) campground on the shore of Fish Lake at ~7,400 ft among aspen and shore willow, ~17 mi up the Steens Mountain Loop Rd from Frenchglen. 23 sites, picnic tables + fire grates, vault toilet + drinking water, no hookups; max RV ~35 ft. First-come, first-served (no reservations); typically open early July-October per snowpack. High-clearance advised on parts of the loop road beyond, but the graded gravel loop to Fish Lake is passable to a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Carter Lake Campground
note: Siuslaw NF, Oregon Dunes NRA. Single loop of 21 sites among shore pine, Sitka spruce and Douglas fir on 28-acre Carter Lake; no hookups, max RV ~30 ft, boat launch. Reservable on recreation.gov (season roughly May-Sep). --Claude

name: Eagle Rock Campground
note: Umpqua NF (Diamond Lake RD) along the North Umpqua River. 27 sites, no hookups, no drinking water, max RV ~30 ft; a majority of sites have river access. Reservable on recreation.gov (season roughly mid-May-Sep). --Claude

name: Frog Lake Campground
note: Mt Hood NF at Frog Lake near Wapinitia Pass. 30 sites (8 tent-only), no hookups, drinking water and vault toilets, max RV ~22 ft (borderline for a 23-ft rig). Reservable on recreation.gov (season roughly late May-mid Sep). --Claude

name: Gone Creek Campground
note: USFS (Mt. Hood NF) campground managed by Portland General Electric on Timothy Lake's south shore. 49 single-family sites (48 standard + 1 double), 18 pull-through, no hookups; RVs to 32 ft. Reservable online; open ~Memorial Day through mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Oak Fork Campground (Timothy Lake)
note: USFS (Mt. Hood NF) campground managed by Portland General Electric on Timothy Lake's south shore, just east of Gone Creek. 36 single-family sites (6 pull-through) plus cabins and hike-to sites; no hookups; RVs to 60 ft. Reservable online; open ~Memorial Day through mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Lake Fork Campground
note: Wallowa-Whitman NF (Pine RD) campground along North Pine/Lake Fork Creek on the paved Hells Canyon Scenic Byway (FR 39), ~8 mi off OR-86 near Halfway. ~10-11 forested sites, hand-pump water, vault toilets, no hookups; first-come, first-served $15. Sites are small and shaded -- larger rigs should scout. Open ~late May through late Oct. --Claude

name: Bull Prairie Lake Campground
note: Umatilla NF (Heppner RD) campground adjacent to 28-acre Bull Prairie Lake (annually trout-stocked; boat ramp, dock, non-motorized boating only, paved accessible lakeshore trail); 28 tent/RV sites plus 2 tent-only, 3 double and 1 group site, potable water, dump station ($10), vault toilets. Reservable online. Maintained Memorial Day to mid-November. Elev ~4050 ft. --Claude

name: Coalmine Hill Campground
note: Umatilla NF (Heppner RD) free FCFS campground atop Coalmine Hill; one larger pull-in site near the entrance plus sites around a large parking area big enough to turn an RV or horse trailer, one vault toilet, a horse corral, and trailhead access to the Willow Creek/Bald Mountain/Hells Half Acre trails; no potable water or garbage service. First-come, first-served. Maintained Memorial Day to mid-November; ~22 mi from Heppner on County Road 678. Elev ~4850 ft. --Claude

name: Spring Creek Campground
note: Small Wallowa-Whitman NF (La Grande RD) campground in open ponderosa pine near a meadow, 12.5 mi NW of La Grande via I-84 exit 248 then FR 21 (1.5 mi). 4 single sites, each with table/fire ring/gravel parking area; no potable water, no hookups. $10/night self-pay, reservable on recreation.gov. Open May-Oct. Open-pine layout with parking pull-ins fits a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Lost Lake Resort & Campground
note: Concessionaire-run campground on Mt. Hood NF land at Lost Lake, 25 mi SW of Hood River. 148 sites across multiple loops; some D-loop sites take RVs to 40 ft, ~64 sites fit 20+ ft rigs. Drinking water, some sewer hookups, boat launch, fishing dock. Reservable on recreation.gov (unreserved go FCFS); open late Apr-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Whispering Falls Campground
note: Willamette NF (Detroit RD) campground next to the North Santiam River in old-growth forest, North Santiam corridor. 16 sites with gravel spurs 30-40 ft (RVs to ~40 ft); drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups. 10 sites reservable on recreation.gov, rest FCFS; open ~May-Sep. RV Life 0*(unrated)/$ (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Poole Creek Campground
note: Umpqua NF campground on the west shore of Lemolo Lake near the mouth of Poole Creek (~4,150 ft), the largest Lemolo Lake campground. 60 standard non-hookup sites plus a group site, vault toilets, drinking water; listed max RV length 45 ft (reviewers note access road/sites suit smaller rigs better). Reservation only on recreation.gov, May-Oct. --Claude

name: Buckhorn Campground
note: Small rustic free Wallowa-Whitman NF campground (~5 sites, ~5,260 ft) on the Zumwalt Prairie rim near Buckhorn Overlook; open ponderosa/grassland. Reached by ~40 mi of gravel Zumwalt/Forest Rd 46, graded and passable by passenger vehicles when dry (not maintained off-season). Vault toilet, no water, FCFS, no fee, June–Sept. --Claude

name: Ollokot Campground
note: Wallowa-Whitman NF campground in old-growth ponderosa along the Wild & Scenic Imnaha River, off FR 39 (Wallowa Mountain Loop Rd, paved); 13 drive-in sites with tables/fire rings/parking, well water, vault toilets, $15/night, primary season June–Sept. --Claude

name: Hart-tish Campground
note: USFS Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Siskiyou Mtns RD) day-use/camp area on the east shore of Applegate Lake, ~0.5 mi below the dam. 7 tent sites plus 8 lakeside dry RV pull-ins (no hookups); rec.gov RV1 lists max RV/trailer 40 ft on a paved back-in, so a 23-ft rig fits easily. Groomed lawn slopes to the lake; store, boat ramp, fish-cleaning station. Reservable online, early May-mid Sept, ~$30/night. --Claude

name: Coverdale Campground
note: USFS Wallowa-Whitman NF (Hells Canyon NRA) small rustic campground along the Wild & Scenic Imnaha River, reached by ~4 mi of FR 3960 gravel off FR 39. 7 standard non-electric sites, both tent and trailer; a few sites fit small RVs, no hookups, no length barrier noted for a 23-ft rig. Reservable on recreation.gov, primarily June-Sept. --Claude

name: Indian Crossing Campground
note: USFS Wallowa-Whitman NF (Wallowa Mountains Office) camp at the end of Forest Rd 3960 on the Wild & Scenic Imnaha River, gateway to the Eagle Cap Wilderness/Hells Canyon NRA. 10 single-family sites (tent/RV/equestrian sections), picnic table + fire ring, no hookups; reservable online, ~$15/night, use season roughly June-Sept. Reached by ~9 mi of maintained gravel forest road. --Claude

name: Topsy Campground
note: BLM (Lakeview District) camp on the upper Klamath River (formerly the shore of J.C. Boyle Reservoir, drained after the 2024 Klamath dam removals) ~1.5 mi off Hwy 66 via gravel Topsy Rd. 13 sites, picnic tables/fire rings, drinking water, vault toilets, RV dump station and boat ramp, no hookups; first-come, first-served, open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Odessa Campground
note: Small free USFS Fremont-Winema NF camp on Odessa Creek at the west edge of Upper Klamath Lake, off Hwy 140 via FR 3639 (~22 mi W of Klamath Falls). 6 sites (listed to 35 ft but rough access road and tight spacing favor shorter rigs; a 23-ft rig fits), picnic tables/fire rings, one vault toilet, no potable water, small-boat ramp; first-come, first-served, open ~mid-May to mid-Dec. --Claude

name: Bull Bend Campground
note: USFS Deschutes NF (Bend-Fort Rock RD) camp on a small peninsula wrapped by a bend of the Deschutes River, south of La Pine off FR 4370. 12 sites, RV/trailer or tent, spurs to ~40 ft, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups; reservable online in season, first-come after late Sept, open ~May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Cottonwood Recreation Area Campground
note: Fremont-Winema NF campground at Cottonwood Meadow Lake NW of Lakeview; ~21-22 sites (a few are walk-in tent-only and one horse site) for tents/RVs/trailers to ~35 ft, piped water, vault toilets, seasonal host, no hookups; lake is non-motorized/electric-only, stocked trout. Snow-free roughly mid-June to mid-Oct; first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Bedrock Campground
note: Willamette NF (Middle Fork RD) campground on a terrace above Fall Creek in the Fall Creek Rec Area E of Lowell; 22 sites including 15 RV sites (max ~30 ft; one site to 40 ft, some short), tent-only sites + 1 ADA, tables/fire rings, hand-pump drinking water, vault toilets, no cell service. Reservable online (recreation.gov), open ~early May-early Sep. --Claude

name: Wildwood Campground
note: Ochoco National Forest, small rustic camp in ponderosa pine/larch/fir east of the Ochoco Divide RNA, reached via FS Rd 2630/2210 off Hwy 26. 5 sites, 24 ft max RV, pit toilets, no water or trash (pack in/out). Free, first-come, first-served, open ~June–Sept. --Claude

name: Bluebill Campground
note: USFS Siuslaw NF, Oregon Dunes NRA (Horsfall area), beside shallow Bluebill Lake. 19 drive-in sites; rec.gov lists per-site max RV lengths of ~41-85 ft, so large rigs fit. No hookups; vault toilets, drinking water. Reservation-only via recreation.gov, open ~May-Sept. OHV access to surrounding dunes. --Claude

name: Islet Campground
note: USFS Willamette NF (Middle Fork RD) campground at the north end of Waldo Lake, just S of North Waldo. 55 sites (31 reservable, rest FCFS), no hookups, vault toilets; RVs to 43 ft. Sandy beaches, boat launch (electric motors only). Open ~June-Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Campbell Lake Campground
note: USFS Fremont-Winema NF (Paisley RD) campground on Campbell Lake in the Gearhart Mountain high country, reached by gravel forest roads. 18 sites, picnic tables/fire rings, 3 vault toilets, potable water, boat launch; no hookups; vehicles to 40 ft. First-come, first-served. Open ~Memorial Day-Labor Day. --Claude

name: Nottingham Campground
note: USFS Mt. Hood NF campground on the East Fork Hood River right off Hwy 35. 21-23 sites, no hookups, vault toilets, no potable water; max vehicle length ~32 ft. Reservable on recreation.gov (some sites FCFS), open ~Memorial Day-September. --Claude

name: Lane Creek Campground
note: Small Umatilla NF campground ~11 mi east of Ukiah off Hwy 244 (North Fork John Day RD). 7 drive-in gravel sites, picnic tables/fire rings, vault toilet, no potable water, pack out trash. Most pads are short but Site 2 fits up to ~40 ft. First-come, first-served; open ~Memorial Day to mid-November. --Claude

name: Edson Creek Campground
note: BLM Coos Bay District (Myrtlewood Field Office) campground ~4 mi up Sixes River Rd from Hwy 101, on Edson Creek near the Sixes River. 27 individual sites plus 5 group sites; no hookups, potable water at kiosk, boat ramp/day-use across the road. Half the main loop is FCFS, half reservable online; group sites reservation-only. Open ~Memorial Day to Sept 30. --Claude

name: Antelope Flat Reservoir Campground
note: Ochoco NF campground at ~5,000 ft on a single loop near 170-acre Antelope Flat Reservoir, ~40 mi SE of Prineville via Hwy 380/FR 17. 23 sites incl pull-through RV spaces, no hookups, hand-pump potable water, vault toilet; boat ramp and day-use at the water's edge. Fee ~$3-8, first-come, first-served, mid-May to mid-Oct. Sites are a short walk back from the water. --Claude

name: Crescent Campground
note: Small rustic Malheur NF (Prairie City RD) campground at ~5,180 ft on the Little (Baby) John Day River, ~17 mi from Prairie City via CR 62. 4 drive-in sites, picnic tables/fire rings, pit toilet, no potable water; a base for the Strawberry Mountain Wilderness. Free, first-come, first-served, ~May-Oct, 14-day limit. Older/rustic facilities. --Claude

name: Jackman Park Campground
note: 6-site BLM (Burns District) campground in an aspen grove at ~7,650 ft on the Steens Mountain Loop Road; vault/universal-access restroom, no potable water; open mid-June-Oct, 14-day limit. Drive-in on the maintained Steens Loop Road. First-come, first-served, $16/night. --Claude

name: South Steens Campground
note: BLM Burns District campground on the west side of Steens Mountain (Steens Mtn Cooperative Management Area). 36 family sites amid juniper/sage plus an adjacent 15-site equestrian loop with corrals; general campground, not equestrian-only. Vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, $16/vehicle; typically open mid-May through mid-November. Trailheads (Big Indian Gorge, Little Blitzen) at the campground. --Claude

name: Double Cabin Campground
note: Small primitive Ochoco National Forest campground in the Maury Mountains, ~5,200 ft, reached via Hwy 380 then gravel FR 16 / FR 16-350. 5 free sites, vault toilet, no potable water; a short walk from Double Cabin Pond. Suited to tents and RVs; typically open May-September; FCFS. --Claude

name: Natural Bridge Campground
note: USFS Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (High Cascades RD), 17 sites on the upper Rogue River at the Natural Bridge lava tube, near Union Creek. No hookups, no potable water; open May-Oct. Scan-and-pay on rec.gov (cashless as of 7/2026); not all sites fit larger RVs, so check site length when booking. --Claude

name: Loon Lake Recreation Site
note: BLM Coos Bay District, 53 sites on 260-acre Loon Lake in the Coast Range ~20 mi ESE of Reedsport. Tent/trailer/RV sites, no hookups; day-use beach, boat launch, swimming. Open Memorial Day-Sept 30; reservable online. --Claude

name: Smith River Falls Campground
note: BLM Coos Bay District, 10 sites on the Smith River just above Smith River Falls, ~26 mi E of Reedsport via Smith River Rd (paved then gravel). First-come, first-served, no fee; picnic tables, fire rings, accessible vault restrooms, boat launch, no drinking water. Open Memorial Day-Sept 30. RV Life 0*/$ unrated (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Vincent Creek Campground
note: BLM Coos Bay District, 5 sites on the Smith River at the mouth of Vincent Creek, ~30 mi E of Reedsport via Smith River Rd. First-come, first-served, no fee; vault restroom, no drinking water, small swimming hole. Open Memorial Day-Sept 30. Satellite shows a riverside clearing with drive-in access. RV Life 0*/$ unrated (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Clearwater Falls Campground
note: Umpqua NF (Diamond Lake RD) small campground on the Clearwater River near Clearwater Falls off Hwy 138. 9 sites (5 off Hwy 138, 4 upper via FR 4785), no hookups, no potable water; $10/night, first-come, first-served (June-Oct). Vehicles 25 ft max due to winding approach. --Claude

name: Hemlock Lake Campground
note: Umpqua NF (North Umpqua RD) campground at 28-acre Hemlock Lake reservoir, reached via ~32 mi of Little River Rd (FR 27) from Glide. 1 double + 9 sites that fit RVs/trailers (to ~35 ft) plus 3 tent-only sites; no hookups, no drinking water; open terrain adjacent to the lake, trout fishing. First-come, first-served (June-Oct). --Claude

name: Cold Springs Campground (OR)
note: Deschutes NF campground ~4 mi west of Sisters on Hwy 242 (McKenzie Pass Hwy); 22 sites, 9 pull-through, no hookups, hand-pump water (seasonal), vault toilets. Large spurs fit big rigs (RVs to 50+ ft). Reservable online. Open ~May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Sixes River Campground
note: BLM Coos Bay District (Myrtlewood FO) campground along the Sixes River E of the coast at Sixes; 19 sites, gravel spurs fit rigs up to ~30 ft, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups; popular for salmon fishing and gold panning; first-come, first-served by self-registration; open Fri before Memorial Day-Sept 30. --Claude

name: Fairview Campground
note: Small 5-site drive-through loop off State Hwy 207 S of Spray, Umatilla NF (Heppner RD); accessible vault toilet, potable water fountain May-Oct; trailhead for 80 mi of OHV routes, used mainly by hunters; FCFS, maintained Memorial Day-mid-Nov. --Claude

name: Rock Creek Reservoir Campground
note: USFS Mt. Hood NF (Barlow RD) campground on the shore of Rock Creek Reservoir, ~30 mi from Government Camp. ~28-33 single-family tent/RV sites, tables and fire rings, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. RVs to 35-40 ft (over 35 ft not recommended). Mix of recreation.gov-reservable and first-come sites; season roughly mid-Apr to mid-Oct. Reservoir fishing (electric motors only), canoeing. --Claude

name: Bear Wallow Creek Campground
note: Small Umatilla NF (North Fork John Day RD) camp on Bear Wallow Creek, ~11.5 mi E of Ukiah off Hwy 244. 8 gravel sites, vault toilets, no potable water/no garbage service; $8/night, first-come, first-served. Open Memorial Day-mid Nov (snow closes access). --Claude

name: Drift Fence Campground
note: Small rustic Umatilla NF hunting camp along FR 52 (Blue Mountain Scenic Byway) S of Ukiah; 6 sites, 2 vault toilets, no potable water/no garbage. Short access road is rough but passable; open Memorial Day-mid Nov, closed only by snow. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Gold Dredge Campground
note: Umatilla NF camp in open ponderosa along the Wild & Scenic North Fork John Day River; from Ukiah S on Hwy 395 ~15 mi then E 7.7 mi on FR 55. 7 sites + group site, vault toilet, no potable water; $8/night, first-come, first-served. Open Memorial Day-mid Nov. Historic Granite 9 mi S. --Claude

name: Dovre Recreation Site
note: BLM Northwest Oregon District (NOT Oregon Dept. of Forestry) on the Nestucca River National Back Country Byway along the Nestucca Wild & Scenic River, W of Willamina. About 10 sites plus a group shelter, paved parking pads, picnic tables/fire rings, two vault toilets, seasonal potable water, no hookups; $15/night. Reservable online or first-come, first-served with on-site payment; season ~May-Sept, no cell reception in the drainage. --Claude

name: Willow Point County Campground (Howard Prairie Lake)
note: Jackson County park on Howard Prairie Lake in the Cascades (elev ~4,600 ft), east of Ashland; 41 campsites, no hookups; boat ramp and fish-cleaning station. Open May-Oct; reservable online/by phone or FCFS. --Claude

name: Barton Park
note: Clackamas County park on the Clackamas River near Barton/Estacada; 112 sites, 103 with water/electric hookups (9 primitive tent), in East and West loops (East loop newer with larger paved sites); showers, dump station, boat ramp. Reservable, open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Baker Bay Park
note: Lane County campground on Dorena Lake (leased from USACE) near Cottage Grove; 48 tent/RV sites incl 5 Premier sites near the water plus 2 group sites, marina/boat ramp, showers, alcohol-free, open ~mid-Apr to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Promontory Park
note: Portland General Electric (investor-owned utility) recreation park on North Fork Reservoir of the Clackamas River, 7 mi east of Estacada; ~50 sites with tent, electric/water RV (rigs to 35 ft), plus cabins and yurts. Store, boat rentals, fishing pier, kids' fishing pond. Alcohol-free; open Memorial Day-Sept, reservable. --Claude

name: Sunnyside County Park
note: Linn County park on Foster Reservoir off Quartzville Rd, ~3 mi off Hwy 20. 130 water/electric hookup sites plus 35 non-hookup sites; 42 sites kept first-come, first-served, rest reservable online. Boat ramp, fish-cleaning station, two stocked ponds. Open early April to early November; big-rig accessible. --Claude

name: Tucker Park
note: Hood River County park on a bend of the Hood River, ~10 min from downtown Hood River off Dee Hwy. 88 sites across upper/lower loops, no hookups (potable water at 20 sites), flush toilets, coin showers; trailers to 30 ft (not all sites fit the max). First-come, first-served, no reservations; open ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: John Neal Memorial Park
note: Linn County park bordering the North Santiam River at Lyons, 30 acres, open April-September. 24 individual sites plus a 12-site group area; 10 RV sites with water hookups (no electric/sewer) and pull-through availability, rest are rustic tent sites. Flush toilets, showers. Reservations required (no FCFS). --Claude

name: Archie Knowles Campground
note: Small Lane County-operated campground on Knowles Creek along Hwy 126, ~4 mi east of Mapleton (on Siuslaw NF land, run by Lane County Parks). 9 tent/RV sites, no hookups, vault toilets, drinking water; RVs up to 40 ft. Sites 7 and 8 are premium creek-view sites. Open Memorial Day-Labor Day, reservable via Lane County. --Claude

name: Depot Park RV Park
note: City of Prairie City park along the Middle Fork John Day River: 20 sites with full hookups (30-amp electric, water, sewer), 10 pull-through, RVs to ~40 ft, big rigs OK, open roughly May-Oct, set in ponderosa pine. Reserve via the host. --Claude

name: Hewitt / Holcomb County Park
note: Baker County park on the Powder River arm of Brownlee Reservoir near Richland; combined Hewitt & John Holcomb parks, ~48 RV/tent sites with paved boat ramps, fish-cleaning stations and a dump station. Open mid-March through Oct 31 with limited FCFS dry camping Nov-Feb. --Claude

name: Crane Prairie Resort
note: Family-run private full-hookup RV park/marina on the NE shore of Crane Prairie Reservoir in the Deschutes NF, ~33 mi SW of Bend on the Cascade Lakes Hwy. 30-amp full-hookup sites, boat ramp/moorage, store; seasonal (snow-closed in winter). Separate from the adjacent USFS Crane Prairie CG. --Claude

name: Lava Lake RV Resort
note: Private full-hookup RV resort on Lava Lake in the Deschutes NF, ~38 mi SW of Bend on the Cascade Lakes Hwy; separate from the adjacent USFS Lava Lake CG. 24 full-hookup sites (electric/water/sewer), showers, laundry, marina/store, boat rentals; seasonal (opens ~June when snow clears), phone reservations only. --Claude

name: River Mountain RV Park
note: Private RV park at 577 Mountain Ave SE in Idanha on the North Fork Santiam River, off Hwy 22 about 3 mi from Detroit Lake. 42 sites with full hookups (50-amp electric, water, sewer), accepts rigs up to ~50 ft; tent sites and rental cabins too. Open ~Apr-Oct, nightly-bookable online. --Claude

name: Richardson Park (Lane County Park)
note: Lane County park campground on the shore of Fern Ridge Reservoir near Junction City/Veneta, the largest developed park in the county system (115 acres). 88 campsites with water/electric (partial hookups), a 212-slip marina, swim area, and day-use; open mid-Apr to mid-Oct, reservable online through Lane County. RV dump station closed during 2026 wastewater upgrades. --Claude

name: East Lake Resort
note: Private lakeside resort (operating since 1915) on East Lake in the Newberry Volcano caldera, ~45 mi SE of Bend. RV area of 40 sites in the lodgepole forest set ~1/4 mi back from the shore: water plus 30-amp (sites 1-27) and 30/50-amp pull-throughs (28-40), no site sewer but a free dump station; back-ins 25-50 ft deep so large rigs fit. Cabins, tent sites, marina/boat rentals, store, and grill on the lake. Seasonal (roughly June-Oct), ~$49/night. --Claude

name: Junipers Reservoir RV Resort
note: Family-owned seasonal (Apr-Oct) RV resort set on a 5,000-acre working cattle ranch overlooking 175-acre Junipers Reservoir, ~7 mi W of Lakeview on Hwy 140; ~45 pull-through sites, electric+water hookups, hot showers, laundry, covered pavilion, lawns. Reservable online/by phone. --Claude

name: PGE Pelton Park
note: Campground operated by Portland General Electric (PGE, an investor-owned utility -> private) on Lake Simtustus, a Deschutes River reservoir near Madras; 67 sites including RV plus yomes/cabins, marina, boat launch, swim area, store/cafe. Open ~3rd Fri in May to 2nd wknd of Sept, reservable online. Access from the N via Hwy 26/Pelton Dam Rd (the S route has a hairpin and one-lane bridge unsuitable for RVs). --Claude

name: Bully Creek Reservoir County Park
note: Malheur County park on Bully Creek Reservoir (Reclamation dam, Vale Oregon Irrigation District water), ~10 mi west of Vale; county-operated since 1966. 40 campsites all with electric hookups (2 ADA), restrooms with showers, dump, two covered shelters, swimming beach and two-lane boat ramp. Open mid-April to mid-Nov; about $25/night. Reclassified from commercial to local (county park). --Claude

name: Pine Hollow Lakeside Resort
note: Private resort on Pine Hollow Reservoir near Wamic (Tygh Valley area). RV sites ($27) and tent sites, plus cabins; water/electric, showers, laundry, store, restaurant/bar, boat rentals. Reservations by phone; open ~Mar 25 through Sept. --Claude

name: Cave Lake State Park - Elk Flat Campground
note: Elk Flat loop up off Success Summit Rd, set back from the lake (first camping area approaching from Hwys 93/50/6); gravel roads + gravel sites, flush toilets + hot showers, open early May-mid-Oct, no hookups. Official max RV 35 ft. All 16 sites reservable on ReserveNevada. --Claude

name: Big Creek Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Austin-Tonopah RD), ~12 mi SW of Austin at the mouth of Big Creek Canyon via FS Rd 002. 8 free FCFS sites, open mid-May-late Oct; no potable water, vault toilets, picnic tables. Fairly open setting; RVs to ~35 ft per FS/reviews but the access road is rough (high-clearance recommended; trailers barred from crossing the top of FSR 002 through-route). RV Life 0*/$ (unrated) (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Kingston Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Austin-Tonopah RD), 12 sites at ~7,100 ft along Kingston Creek in Kingston Canyon in the Toiyabe Range. Free, first-come, first-served, open mid-May-late Oct; picnic tables, fire pits, vault toilets, no potable water. RVs to ~35 ft but the final 2.5-mi single-lane dirt road is tight for big rigs - scout sites on foot. RV Life 0*/$ (unrated) (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Toquima Cave Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Austin-Tonopah RD), small free primitive campground at ~7,900 ft in Pete's Canyon/Midas Canyon of the Toquima Range, ~20 mi SE of Austin off SR-376. 5 sites, trailers up to 25 ft; vault toilets, picnic tables, no potable water; open mid-May-late Oct via graded dirt forest road. Half-mile trail to Toquima Cave pictographs. First-come, first-served. RV Life 0*/$ (unrated) (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Baker Creek Campground (Great Basin National Park)
note: NPS Great Basin NP, ~3 mi down gravel Baker Creek Rd off the Lehman Caves entrance road. ~37 sites at ~7,500 ft; Lower Loop takes RVs/trailers (some sites to ~50 ft), Upper Loop (9-14) is no-RV. $20/night; reservable via recreation.gov Jun-early Aug, otherwise first-come, first-served (open ~mid-May-late Sep). Vault toilets, fire grills, no potable water. --Claude

name: Jack Creek Campground
note: USFS Humboldt-Toiyabe NF, Mountain City-Ruby Mtns-Jarbidge RD. Small free campground on the banks of Jack Creek below Jacks Peak; RVs to 25 ft, vault toilets, tables, fire rings, no water. Reached off paved roads via BLM/ranch gravel. First-come first-served, ~May-Nov. --Claude

name: Wildhorse Crossing Campground
note: USFS Humboldt-Toiyabe NF, Mountain City-Ruby Mtns-Jarbidge RD. ~19 sites in the Owyhee River canyon on NV-225, ~68 mi N of Elko and just N of Wildhorse Reservoir; tables, fire rings/grills, vault toilets, trash, no water. Trailers/RVs to ~35 ft. $5/night, first-come first-served, ~May-Nov (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Bird Creek Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Ely RD), Duck Creek Basin high on the Schell Creek Range at ~8,200 ft. 10 sites (single, double and a group day-use site); 6 sites take RVs/trailers 15-34 ft. Vault toilets, seasonal potable water. Reservable online. Open ~late May-mid Oct. Maintained gravel Duck Creek Basin access. --Claude

name: East Creek Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Ely RD), Duck Creek Basin on the Schell Creek Range. 12 newly-improved sites with tables, fire rings/grills, vault toilets; no potable water (pack in/out). $5/night, reservable online. East Creek (perennial trout stream) runs through the picnic area. Maintained Duck Creek Basin Rd access; open ~late May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Kalamazoo Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Ely RD), small campground adjacent to Kalamazoo Creek on the east side of the Schell Creek Range. 8 sites with tables, fire rings, BBQ pedestals; no potable water. Free (FCFS, not on recreation.gov). Per fs page accommodates full-sized RVs in dry weather, but the access road is bumpy/narrow and high-clearance/4WD is advised when wet. Open ~late May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Jarbidge Campground
note: Small primitive Humboldt-Toiyabe NF campground at the historic town of Jarbidge (~6,350 ft) in Jarbidge Canyon, NE Nevada; a handful of sites best for small/medium rigs (~22-24 ft, comparable to nearby Sawmill), vault toilet, no potable water. Free, first-come, first-served, open ~June-Oct once the canyon road clears. Reached via the long graded Jarbidge Canyon Rd - remote but passable by a normal vehicle. --Claude

name: Sawmill Campground
note: Small rustic Humboldt-Toiyabe NF campground ~1 mi N of Jarbidge (~6,100 ft) in Jarbidge Canyon; 5 sites for small/medium vehicles, trailers/motorhomes to under ~25 ft (EKKO 23 ft fits, tight), vault toilets, fire rings, no potable water. Free, first-come, first-served, open ~June-Oct. Reached via graded Jarbidge Canyon Rd - remote but passable by a normal vehicle. --Claude

name: Thomas Canyon Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Ruby Mtns), at the mouth of Thomas Canyon in Lamoille Canyon ~30 mi SE of Elko, ~7,200 ft. 39 single/double sites (3 pull-through), no hookups, vault toilets, drinking water; Loop A best for larger rigs, sites accept RVs to ~65 ft (Loops B/C have tight turns). Reservable on recreation.gov mid-May to early Sept. --Claude

name: Hilltop Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF, Spring Mountains NRA, upper Kyle Canyon (Mount Charleston) ~40 mi from Las Vegas, ~8,400 ft. 35 single/double sites, no hookups, no potable water, vault toilets, paved spurs. Trailers over 25 ft not recommended due to tight turns (23-ft rig OK). Odd sites reservable on recreation.gov, even sites FCFS; open May-Nov. --Claude

name: Peavine Creek Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Austin-Tonopah RD) drive-in campground in Peavine Canyon on the SE side of the Toiyabe Range near the Arc Dome Wilderness, ~2,080 m. FS lists it as a drive-in facility accommodating RVs up to 35 ft, open ~May-Oct, vault toilet, tables, no potable water. Access is ~9 mi of dirt road off SR-376 (graded, normal-vehicle passable). First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Pine Creek Campground (Toquima)
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Austin-Tonopah RD) campground on the east side of the Toquima Range in Monitor Valley, ~2,320 m (7,510 ft), at the edge of the Alta Toquima Wilderness. 21 sites (about 14 drive-in sites along the creek plus ~6 walk-in), pit toilets, tables, fire rings, no potable water; popular with hunters. Open ~May-Nov. Access is graded dirt road (normal-vehicle passable). First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Nevada Beach Campground
note: USFS Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit campground on the Nevada shore of Lake Tahoe, just north of Stateline. ~54 sites in pine-forest loops set behind a sandy beach; picnic tables, fire rings/grills, flush toilets and drinking water; no hookups. RVs to ~45 ft. Reservable on recreation.gov, roughly late May through mid-October; 14-day stay limit. --Claude

name: White River Campground
note: Small rustic Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Ely Ranger District) campground ~30 mi west of Ely, then 9.5 mi in on graded gravel NFSR-405. 5 dispersed-style sites along the White River with picnic tables and fire rings; vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups. Free, first-come, first-served; open roughly late May through mid-October. Reviewers note lots of flat ground; graded gravel access. RV Life 0*/$ (auto 7/2026, unrated). --Claude

name: Lower Lehman Creek Campground
note: NPS campground in Great Basin National Park along Lehman Creek at ~7,300 ft; 9 sites (6 large paved pull-throughs), max RV/trailer 40 ft, vault toilets, no hookups, $20/night. Reservable on recreation.gov during peak season (late May-early Sep), first-come first-served the rest of the year. --Claude

name: Sunrise Valley RV Park
note: Small transient RV park on US-95 at the south edge of Mina, base of Pilot Mountain (ATV trail access, 500+ mi of trails). ~15-26 sites, mostly full-hookup pull-throughs, clean restrooms/showers, laundry, free WiFi; seasonal (open ~Mar-Oct). Reservable. --Claude

name: Cottonwood Campground (Canyon de Chelly National Monument)
note: Campground at Canyon de Chelly NM (NPS unit on Navajo land; run by the Navajo Nation Tseyi' Dine Heritage Area), ~93 sites, no hookups, water and flush toilets, dump station on exit. First-come, first-served for individual sites (group sites reservable); cash-drop fee ~$20/RV. Open roughly Apr-Oct. Drive-in sites fit RVs. --Claude

name: Pine Grove Campground
note: Coconino NF (Flagstaff RD), off Lake Mary Rd/FH3 ~19 mi SE of Flagstaff in tall pines. 46 single sites (24 reservable, rest FCFS), 16 fully accessible, RVs/trailers to 42 ft, no hookups but coin showers and an RV dump station on site, potable water for registered campers. Summer season. Near Upper/Lower Lake Mary and Ashurst/Marshall lakes. --Claude

name: DeMotte Campground
note: Kaibab NF (North Kaibab RD), on AZ-67 ~7 mi N of the Grand Canyon North Rim entrance (~8,800 ft) beside DeMotte Park meadow. 38 single sites in two loops, RVs to 40 ft, no hookups, vault toilets, limited potable water (no RV-tank fills). Half reservable via recreation.gov, half FCFS; mid-May-mid-Oct (road closed in winter). --Claude

name: Desert View Campground
note: NPS campground on the South Rim, 23 mi east of Grand Canyon Village near Desert View Watchtower. ~50 dry sites (no hookups/water/sewer), picnic table + fire grill each, two water faucets. RVs/trailers to 30 ft total. Reservation-required in season (mid-Apr to mid-Oct) via recreation.gov, no FCFS held back. Elev ~7,463 ft. --Claude

name: Tonto National Forest, Tortilla Campground
note: Tonto NF winter campground (open Oct-Apr) on the Apache Trail (AZ-88) near Tortilla Flat and Canyon Lake; 77 sites, flush toilets and a dump station, max RV ~32 ft; sites 55-59 reservable, the rest first-come, first-served. Closed for an extensive repair - not taking reservations for the 2026-2027 winter season until further notice (per recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Mogollon Campground
note: Tonto NF, atop the Mogollon Rim off FR 300 (Rim Road) ~4 mi from SR 260 (Payson RD), ~7,650 ft. 26 sites, RVs/trailers to 32 ft, drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups. First-come, first-served; open ~May-Oct. Rim Country lakes (Woods Canyon) ~15 min E. --Claude

name: FR 9350 Dispersed Camping
note: Apache-Sitgreaves NF designated dispersed camping along Forest Road 9350, a ~2-mi dirt spur off well-graded FR 300 (Rim Road) atop the Mogollon Rim near Heber. ~42 primitive marked sites spread over ~1.25 mi, many with rim views; two vault toilets near the Carr Lake trailhead, metal fire rings, no water/hookups. Free, first-come, first-served, 14-day limit; open roughly May-Nov (impassable after snowfall). Some sites sit near a ~200-ft rim drop-off. --Claude

name: Canyon Vista Campground
note: Coconino NF campground ~6 mi southeast of Flagstaff on Lake Mary Rd (FH-3), in ponderosa/mixed conifer near Walnut Canyon and Lower Lake Mary. 14 single-unit sites, fire rings, grills, tables, potable water, vault toilets, no hookups; motorhomes/trailers over 40 ft not permitted. Combination reservable (Recreation.gov) + first-come, first-served; open early May-mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Rim Campground
note: Apache-Sitgreaves NF (Black Mesa RD) at the Mogollon Rim edge on FR-300, ~1 mi off SR-260, at ~7,540 ft; known for 100-mile rim views. 26 sites (1-13 FCFS, 14-26 reservable online), no hookups, RVs to 32 ft; drinking water and vault toilets. Woods Canyon Lake ~3 mi. Open ~mid-May through Labor Day weekend. --Claude

name: Molino Basin Campground
note: Coronado NF (Santa Catalina RD) campground at ~4,300 ft on the Catalina Hwy up Mt Lemmon, ~10 mi NE of Tucson. 37 sites off paved roads, 2WD/low-clearance accessible; no hookups, no potable water. Trailers/RVs listed to 22 ft (borderline for a 23-ft rig — a few of the larger sites fit). Open Nov 1–early May (low-elevation winter site). Reservable online. --Claude

name: Double Springs Campground
note: Coconino NF campground in a grassy draw near Mormon Lake (~7,100 ft), ~25 mi SE of Flagstaff. 15 single-unit sites with gravel pads, potable water, no hookups; max RV 35 ft. Reservable on recreation.gov, open ~May-Oct. Lake View Trail from the campground climbs to overlooks of Mormon Lake. --Claude

name: Lakeview Campground
note: Coconino NF campground on a rise above the south shore of Upper Lake Mary, ~13 mi SE of Flagstaff (~6,960 ft). 30 sites (15 reservable / 15 FCFS), drinking water, no hookups; tents and small motorhomes/RVs to ~28 ft. Boat ramp nearby; open ~May-mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Lower Wolf Creek Campground
note: Prescott NF, on the banks of Wolf Creek south of Prescott. 20 CCC-built sites with tables and fire rings; no hookups, no drinking water, vault toilets. First-come, first-served, $10/night; open Memorial Day weekend through Oct 31. Sites accommodate trailers ~22-40 ft; graded-dirt/FR-97 access. (Temporarily closed for bear activity at time of research.) --Claude

name: Raccoon Campground
note: Apache-Sitgreaves NF (Alpine RD), one of the East Fork Black River Recreation Area campgrounds ~13 mi from Alpine via graveled FR 249/FR 276. ~10 sites, $14/night, concessionaire-operated, first-come first-served (not reservable), vault toilet, no potable water; East Fork of the Black River runs ~50 yds south. Sites are small and only some fit larger rigs. Open roughly mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Cunningham Campground
note: Coronado NF (Safford RD) high campground on Mount Graham at ~9,000 ft, ~29 mi up the Swift Trail/AZ-366 (paved to Columbine) across from the Columbine work center. About 10 sites in an open aspen/fir stand around a parking loop; vault toilet, no hookups. Max RV length 22 ft (some sites shorter). First-come, first-served, $10/night, mid-April to mid-November. --Claude

name: Spencer Canyon Campground
note: Coronado NF (Santa Catalina RD) campground on Mount Lemmon at ~8,000 ft, ~21.5 mi up the paved Catalina Hwy. 66 sites with concrete tables, fire pits, bear boxes; no hookups. Tents, trailers to 22 ft, and small motorhomes permitted. First-come, first-served, concessionaire-operated (Recreation Resource Management), open ~April-October. --Claude

name: Forked Pine Campground
note: 24 single-family sites on the east/south shore of Ashurst Lake in Coconino NF; 14 reservable online and 10 first-come, first-served. Vault toilets, seasonal drinking water, no hookups. Some sites take RVs to ~32-35 ft. Reached via ~4 mi graded/maintained dirt FR 82E off Lake Mary Rd. Open roughly early May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Horse Springs Campground
note: Apache-Sitgreaves NF (Alpine RD) campground in ponderosa pine along the East Fork of the Black River, ~13 mi via FR 249/276 from Alpine; 27 single sites, no hookups, vault toilets, drinking water, group ramada. RVs to 32 ft. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov); open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Kehl Springs Campground
note: Small primitive Coconino NF campground on the Mogollon Rim off FR 300 (Rim Road) at ~7,440 ft; 8 sites, vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups. Gravel-road drive-in. Small rigs only, listed max RV length ~22 ft (borderline for a 23-ft rig). First-come, first-served; seasonal early May-late Oct. --Claude

name: Knoll Lake Campground
note: Coconino NF campground on a forested bench above Knoll Lake on the Mogollon Rim; ~24-30 sites for tents and RVs, RVs accommodated to ~32 ft, vault toilets, potable water, no hookups. Graveled forest-road access (FR 295E, rough/switchbacks but sedan-passable). First-come, first-served; seasonal May-Oct. --Claude

name: Watson Lake Park
note: City of Prescott lakeside park in the Granite Dells on Watson Lake; 35 campsites (19 reservable, remainder first-come, first-served), tent/RV, no hookups, restrooms with showers, picnic table/fire pit/grill each site. Open ~1st weekend of April through 1st weekend of October, Thu-Mon nights only; $25/site, max stay 3 days. --Claude

name: Horseshoe Cienega Lake Campground
note: White Mountain Apache Tribe (Fort Apache Reservation) campground on 121-acre Horseshoe Cienega Lake, ~70 sites in ponderosa forest, no hookups; potable water, vault toilets, dump station. Drive-in off AZ-260 east of McNary. Seasonal (~May-Oct), first-come, first-served on a tribal recreation/camping permit (buy online or by phone). --Claude

name: Wheatfields Lake Campground
note: Navajo Nation campground on the shore of Wheatfields Lake in the Chuska Mountains (~7,300 ft), on paved Navajo Route 12. Drive-in RV sites (reported to 45 ft) among pinyon/ponderosa along the north/east shore; some hookups, tent sites and cabins, vault toilets, no potable water on site. Open roughly May-Oct; Navajo camping permit required (and a Navajo fishing license to fish the trout lake). --Claude

name: Albee Creek Campground (Humboldt Redwoods State Park)
note: Drive-in family campground on Mattole Rd in Humboldt Redwoods SP, in a meadow/redwood setting. ~40 sites (about 23 accommodate RVs/trailers), no hookups; RVs/trailers limited to 24 ft max. Seasonal (roughly May-Oct); reservable online. --Claude

name: Mill Creek Campground (Del Norte Coast Redwoods SP)
note: The one developed car campground in Del Norte Coast Redwoods SP (part of Redwood National & State Parks), ~2 mi east of US-101 up Mill Creek Rd in old-growth/second-growth redwoods. 145 sites in Northern (75-145) and Southern (1-74) loops, no hookups but a dump/water fill station; RVs to ~28 ft and trailers to ~24 ft (some sources up to 31 ft). Reservable online, open roughly May-Sept. --Claude

name: Grover Hot Springs State Park Campground
note: California State Parks campground in Hot Springs Valley ~4 mi W of Markleeville (Alpine County), elev ~6000 ft. 76 forested family sites (Hot Springs / Toiyabe loops); no hookups; max ~27 ft motorhomes / 24 ft trailers. Summer camping ~mid-May to mid-Sep, reservable via ReserveCalifornia. Reopened for camping after the 2021 Tamarack Fire; recovering well per 2025-26 reviews (hot-springs pool open limited days). --Claude

name: Jackson Demonstration State Forest (Camp 1)
note: Coastal-redwood state demonstration forest (Cal Fire) ~6 mi east of Fort Bragg off Hwy 20; rustic drive-in campsites in the Camp 1 cluster (Redtail/Wagon/Roundhouse/Tin Can loops), seasonal mid-May to Sept, pit toilets, no water or hookups. First-come, first-served with self-registration. --Claude

name: Mountain Home Demonstration State Forest, Frazier Mill Campground
note: CAL FIRE demonstration state forest campground at ~6,150 ft among giant sequoias, reached via the narrow winding Balch Park Rd/Bear Creek Rd from Springville (~21 mi). 46 sites, 14 suitable for RVs/trailers up to 35 ft; no hookups, water spigots, vault toilets, bear boxes. First-come, first-served (ADA site C2 reservable by phone). Season mid-May-October. --Claude

name: Doane Valley Campground (Palomar Mountain State Park)
note: California State Parks. 31 wooded sites at ~4700 ft on Palomar Mtn; RVs to 27 ft, trailers to 24 ft; no hookups, no dump station. Vault/flush toilets, water. Open ~May-Oct, reservable via ReserveCalifornia. --Claude

name: Russian Gulch State Park
note: Coastal Mendocino state park 2 mi N of Mendocino; campground sits in the redwood creek canyon E of Hwy 1, reached by a one-lane road under the Hwy 1 bridge. 26 standard drive-in sites (+4 equestrian, 1 group); RVs/trailers to 24 ft, no hookups; flush toilets and showers. Reservable May–Labor Day via ReserveCalifornia; separate coastal cove/headland day-use area. --Claude

name: Agua Caliente County Park
note: San Diego County desert park in the Anza-Borrego area with natural hot springs. ~140 sites across several loops: full-hookup, partial-hookup, and no-hookup RV/trailer sites plus tent sites; flush toilets, showers, dump station. Seasonally operated (open ~Labor Day to Memorial Day; closed summer heat). Reservable online through San Diego County Parks. --Claude

name: Baker Creek Campground
note: Inyo County campground in a meadow along Baker Creek just west of Big Pine (Eastern Sierra, off US-395). ~40 sites, no hookups, vault toilets, no showers; $14/night. Sites vary - some fit 30-ft rigs, others small/unlevel, so pick a larger site for a 23-ft rig. Mix of FCFS and reservable. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Del Mar Fairgrounds RV Park
season_source: note prose (cleaned out of the note 2026-10-14)
note: Two RV lots on the Del Mar Fairgrounds (22nd District Agricultural Association), minutes from the beach: Surf & Turf RV Park (60 sites) and the fairgrounds' own RV lot (58 spaces), all back-in with full hookups.  Restrooms and laundry.  Daily and weekly stays, booked up to 2 months ahead, 21 nights a calendar year at most.  Closed in summer for the San Diego County Fair and the racing season. --Claude

name: Balch Park Campground
note: Tulare County park inholding surrounded by CAL FIRE's Mountain Home Demonstration State Forest, ~6,000 ft in the giant-sequoia belt NE of Springville. Two campgrounds on Balch Park Rd — Lower and Upper Balch Park — plus two stocked fishing ponds; no hookups, RVs/trailers to 40 ft. First-come, first-served; open seasonally ~mid-May to mid-Nov. Distinct from the CAL FIRE Frazier Mill Campground ~2 km NW. --Claude

name: Navy Camp (Lake Pillsbury)
note: PG&E-operated Lake Pillsbury campground in Mendocino NF; single loop of ~20 sites with paved parking aprons under valley oaks, vault toilets, no hookups; posted vehicle max ~22 ft (pads ~12x25 ft, borderline for a 23-ft rig). First-come, first-served, open ~May-Sept. Lake Pillsbury reservoir and its recreation facilities are slated for removal under PG&E's Potter Valley Project decommissioning (dam removal proposed ~2028+); currently operating. --Claude  All sites first-come, first-served; no reservations (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Fuller Grove Campground (Lake Pillsbury)
note: PG&E-operated campground on the west shore of Lake Pillsbury (Mendocino NF); ~23 individual sites (incl. six doubles) plus a reservable group site, paved aprons (the more RV-friendly of the Pillsbury camps), boat ramp and beach access, vault toilets, no hookups. Individual sites first-come, first-served (group site reservable online); open ~May-Sept. Reservoir/facilities slated for removal under PG&E's Potter Valley Project decommissioning; currently operating. --Claude  All sites first-come, first-served; no reservations (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Oak Bottom Campground (Salmon River)
note: Six Rivers NF campground on a wooded slope above the California/Salmon River near Somes Bar; 25 single-family sites with bear lockers, picnic tables and fire rings, vault toilets and drinking water, dry camping (no hookups), trailers to 35 ft. Reservable ~mid-May through mid-Oct. Popular spring whitewater put-in. --Claude

name: Manzanita Lake Campground
note: Largest campground in Lassen Volcanic NP (~179 sites incl. RV sites, no hookups) at ~5,900 ft by Manzanita Lake; flush/vault toilets, dump station, camp store; RVs to ~35 ft, reservable via recreation.gov (roughly late May-Oct). --Claude

name: Shafter Campground
note: Klamath NF (Goosenest RD) campground in Butte Valley beside trout-stocked Butte Creek; ~10 sites, vault toilets, no potable water, dump available, $10/night, first-come, first-served, RVs to about 40 ft. Open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Rocky Knoll Campground
note: Developed Lassen NF campground near the east shore of Silver Lake (Caribou Wilderness trailheads nearby); 18 sites, some able to accommodate RVs, with tables, fire rings and vault toilets; hand-pump water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (no reservations); typically open June-Sept. --Claude

name: Silver Bowl Campground
note: Developed Lassen NF campground near the shore of Silver Lake with a nearby boat ramp (Caribou Wilderness trailheads adjacent); 18 sites, some RV-capable, with tables, fire rings and vault toilets; no hookups. First-come, first-served (no reservations); typically open June-Sept. --Claude

name: White Wolf Campground
note: Yosemite NP campground at ~2435 m off Tioga Rd (Hwy 120), a short paved spur north; 74 sites, vault toilets, drinking water; RVs to 27 ft / trailers to 24 ft at some sites (many sites smaller, so book per site). Reservable via Recreation.gov, typically mid-June to mid-September. --Claude

name: Sand Bar Flat Campground
note: Stanislaus NF (Summit RD) forested campground on the Middle Fork Stanislaus River; 10 sites, vault toilets, no potable water (bring your own); max RV/trailer 35 ft, though the steep, narrow unpaved road past Fraser Flat is not advisable for large rigs. First-come, first-served, not on Recreation.gov. Open ~April-December. RV Life 0*/$ (auto 7/2026, unrated). --Claude

name: Pine City Campground
note: Small Inyo NF campground in the Mammoth Lakes Basin near Lake Mary, ~8,900 ft, on the paved Lake Mary Rd; 10 sites, no hookups, first-come, first-served, open summer only. Accommodates tents and smaller RVs. --Claude

name: Troy Meadow
note: Sequoia NF (Kern Plateau) campground at ~7,800 ft off Sherman Pass Rd (22S05, paved); 73 sites with paved spurs, no trailer-length limit, vault toilets, non-potable water, bear boxes, OHV-trail access. First-come, first-served, open May-Nov. --Claude

name: Sunset Campground
note: Death Valley NP. 270-site campground near Furnace Creek laid out as a large gravel/paved lot, open roughly Oct-Apr; big-rig friendly (open pull-through spots) with no hookups (potable water and dump station nearby). First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Stovepipe Wells Campground
note: Death Valley NP. ~190-site gravel campground across from Stovepipe Wells Village, open roughly Oct-Apr; large open lot that fits big rigs, no hookups (dump station and water at the village; a separate private RV park there has hookups). First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Eagle Creek Campground
note: Shasta-Trinity NF campground on the upper Trinity River near the Eagle Creek confluence, Hwy 3 north of Trinity Center, 17-18 sites, drinking water, vault toilets, RVs/trailers to 35 ft; open roughly mid-May to late August. --Claude

name: Idlewild Campground
note: 11 sites on the North Fork Salmon River, Salmon/Scott River RD, Klamath NF, ~20 mi west of Etna on Sawyers Bar Rd; vault toilets, summer potable water, fire rings, max RV about 24 ft; first-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov), 14-day limit, open ~May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Curly Jack Campground
note: On the Klamath Wild & Scenic River off Curly Jack Rd near Happy Camp, Happy Camp RD, Klamath NF; 16 single sites (most fit ~24 ft, some to 40 ft) plus 4 group sites, vault toilets, potable water, shaded paved loops; individual sites first-come, first-served (groups reservable on recreation.gov), open ~mid May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Butte Meadows Campground
note: Along Butte Creek in the Butte Meadows community, Almanor RD, Lassen NF; 13 drive-in sites (paved Humboldt Rd access, road rough in spots), picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, ~$12/night self-pay; first-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov), open ~April-Oct. --Claude

name: Potato Patch Campground
note: On Highway 32 along Deer Creek, Almanor RD, Lassen NF; ~30-32 sites, drive-in off the paved highway, drinking water, vault toilets, fire rings, no hookups; first-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov), open ~April-Nov. --Claude

name: Honn Campground
note: Small primitive Lassen NF campground on Hat Creek along Hwy 89 (Hat Creek RD); 6 shady streamside sites with fire rings/BBQs and vault toilets, no potable water; flat drive-in access directly off the highway. First-come, first-served, $10/night, open ~April-October. --Claude

name: Soldier Meadows Campground
note: Lassen NF (Almanor RD) primitive developed campground in a meadow near Soldier Creek at ~4,890 ft, reached by forest roads; 15 sites, vault toilets, no potable water, $10/night, first-come, first-served; open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Domingo Springs Campground
note: Lassen NF (Almanor RD) developed drive-in campground, 18 sites along the North Fork Feather River near the PCT; vault toilets, potable water, max 2 vehicles/8 people per site; FCFS (fee paid on arrival), open ~May-Sep. --Claude

name: Goumaz Campground
note: Lassen NF (Eagle Lake RD) small drive-in campground, 5 sites on the Susan River beside the Bizz Johnson Trail; vault toilet, seasonal potable water, free FCFS; Hwy 44 access recommended when towing trailers, open ~May-Oct. --Claude
